title: SAVEPOINT
description: A SAVEPOINT marks a point inside a transaction you can roll back to later, without undoing everything before it. Create a savepoint named `before_raise`, then give every employee a $1000 raise (UPDATE salary = salary + 1000).
hints: SAVEPOINT <name> just marks a point in time within the current transaction - it doesn't change any data by itself, it's only useful once you later ROLLBACK TO it.
SAVEPOINT before_raise, as its own statement, then a normal UPDATE employees SET salary = salary + 1000.
expected_behavior: Every employee's salary increases by 1000; the savepoint itself changes nothing on its own.
solution: SAVEPOINT before_raise; UPDATE employees SET salary = salary + 1000;
explanation: A SAVEPOINT is cheap to create and doesn't commit anything - it's purely a bookmark inside the current transaction that ROLLBACK TO can later return to.

hidden_tests.check_query: SELECT first_name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY id
hidden_tests.label: every employee got the raise
